column1: # Can the model-routing rules live in their own HTTPRoutes?
# Every Gateway API cap is PER ROUTE - 16 rules, 64 matches per rule, 128 matches
# per route - and nothing caps how many routes attach to a Gateway. So the budget
# is only a budget if all the matches have to be in one route, and they do not.
# Shape probed: three HTTPRoutes, each carrying ONE model-routing rule for one
# model, all backendRef'ing svc-a's InferencePool, on /shard/v1/chat/completions
# so they do not collide with the fixture's own route. Rule name deliberately
# IDENTICAL in all three, to see whether sharding inherits #282.
# manifests/shard-probe.yaml, applied to the istio gateway, real vLLM backends.
# MEASURED: does each shard resolve, and is the right adapter served?
shard
shard-1
shard-2
shard-3
# MEASURED: does adding routes cost any existing route its endpoint-picker config?
# This is the istio#58392 failure mode - ext_proc lost for all but the first route
# when several merge on one gateway. Envoy config_dump, before and after.
state
before
after
# +3 routes, +3 with ext_proc. Nothing lost. Each shard route carries its own
# per-route ext_proc config, so the picker is in the path for all of them.
# istio 1.30.3, which has the istio#58393 fix. On 1.28.1-1.28.4 this is exactly
# the shape that breaks.
# MEASURED: the three shards share one rule name. Did their EPP configs collide?
check
distinct ext_proc configs across the 3 shards
clusters
verdict
column2: benign HERE because all three target the SAME pool. Shards spanning
different pools would hit #282, so shard rule names must be unique.

one rule per shard
one rule per endpoint per shard
